events.event: BEI data showed the IHSG fell 3.71% in the week of 16-20 November to 5,146.33 and market capitalisation dropped to Rp8,725 trillion, while foreign investors' cumulative 2026 net sell passed Rp100 trillion.
events.key_numbers: IHSG 5,344.41 to 5,146.33 (-3.71% w/w) · market cap Rp9,047T to Rp8,725T (-3.56%, about Rp322T lost) · foreign net sell Fri 20 Nov Rp947.41B · foreign net sell YTD Rp100.235T · avg daily value Rp12.35T (-47.9%) · Bloomberg IDX Foreign Flow Index -US$5.68B · IHSG about -40% YTD
events.why_it_matters: Foreign money leaving at record pace hits stock portfolios, pension funds and the rupiah.
events.spreading_evidence: Top headline on detik bursa page 21 Nov; covered by many outlets

events.event: OJK board chair Friderica Widyasari Dewi said the IHSG's fall from about 9,134 in January 2026 to around 5,000 is a logical consequence of capital market reforms such as removing high-concentration stocks and aligning the index with MSCI, and urged investors not to panic.
events.key_numbers: IHSG peak about 9,134 (Jan 2026) · now about 5,100-5,200 · eight reform steps cited · HSC stocks removed from IHSG calculation
events.why_it_matters: The regulator's own explanation for a roughly 43% drop in the index many ordinary investors hold.
events.spreading_evidence: Two detik pieces (19 and 20 Nov), several regional outlets

events.event: Bank Indonesia Governor Destry Damayanti said BI is giving up to 45% discount on hedging costs (DNDF/swap) to pull foreign capital back into Indonesian assets, with US$14.1 billion of hedging transactions so far.
events.key_numbers: discount up to 45% on DNDF · hedging transactions US$14.1B (June to 17 Nov 2026) · stock outflow YTD Rp81.6T · SBN+SRBI inflow YTD Rp143T
events.why_it_matters: BI is paying to keep the rupiah from sliding further past Rp18,300, which affects import prices.

events.event: The rupiah moved close to Rp18,300 per US dollar on 20-21 November and analysts expect continued pressure next week despite BI's rate hike.
events.key_numbers: USD/IDR about Rp18,270-18,297 (20 Nov) · BI Rate 6.00% · detik headline 'Makin Dekat ke Rp18.300'
events.why_it_matters: A weaker rupiah raises prices of imported goods, fuel and electronics.

events.event: Anthropic priced its Nasdaq IPO (ticker ANT) at US$83 per share, above the US$70-78 range, raising about US$81.3 billion and valuing the company around US$1.1 trillion, equal to about 84% of Indonesia's GDP and 2.2 times the IDX market cap.
events.key_numbers: IPO price US$83 (range US$70-78) · 980M shares offered · raise about US$81.34B (about Rp1,484.6T) · market value about US$1.1T (about Rp20,000T) · 2.2x BEI market cap (Rp9,047T) · first-day close reportedly US$97.17 (+17.1%) · public float about 7% · Indonesian retail cannot buy at IPO price
events.why_it_matters: One AI company is now worth more than twice the whole Indonesian stock market, and the IDX is losing foreign money while the world buys AI.
events.spreading_evidence: Multiple detik/CNBC/IDN pieces; comparison to PDB RI in headline

events.event: Indonesia and the European Union signed the IEU-CEPA trade deal and an Investment Protection Agreement in Brussels after about 10 years of talks, targeting entry into force on 1 January 2027.
events.key_numbers: 90.4% of Indonesian tariff lines at 0% on entry into force · 8.37% phased over 3-15 years · duty-free CPO quota 1.9M tonnes (+140,000 t palm oil) · trade about US$30B/year · EU investment about US$25B in 5 years · 72 GI products protected · EU Parliament debate begins 23 Nov
events.why_it_matters: Cheaper access to the EU for palm oil, garments and footwear exporters, and cheaper imported machinery.

events.event: The European Parliament is scheduled to begin debating ratification of the IEU-CEPA on 23 November, with both sides needing to ratify before the 1 January 2027 target as Indonesia's EU GSP preferences end on 31 December 2026.
events.key_numbers: EP debate 23 Nov 2026 · GSP ends 31 Dec 2026 · target entry into force 1 Jan 2027
events.why_it_matters: Exporters risk a tariff gap in January if ratification slips.

events.event: Nasdaq plans to station a team at the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) from December to help strengthen trading surveillance, as BEI tightens oversight and reports 34.3 million capital market investors.
events.key_numbers: Nasdaq team at BEI from December 2026 · investors 34.3 million · six companies reported queuing for IPO (detik 21 Nov)
events.why_it_matters: An attempt to win back foreign trust after MSCI doubts about manipulation and transparency.

events.event: Brent crude closed at US$92.57 per barrel on 20 November, down 3.41% on the week and a third straight weekly decline, as Hormuz shipments recovered; OPEC+ meets 29 November on 2027 quotas.
events.key_numbers: Brent Jan US$92.57 (-3.41% w/w; US$95.84 on 13 Nov) · WTI about US$83.41 (-5% w/w) · Goldman sees 2027 surplus about 2M bpd, Brent avg about US$88 · OPEC+ meeting 29 Nov
events.why_it_matters: Lower oil eases pressure on the subsidy budget and on the rupiah, but subsidised fuel prices are frozen through 31 Dec anyway.

events.event: The Ministry of Forestry revoked the forest utilisation permit (PBPH) of PT RAPP (Group APRIL) over 338,536 hectares via decree 971/2026, announced by Satgas PKH; the government says operations will move to a BUMN/BUMD arrangement with no mass layoffs.
events.key_numbers: 338,536 ha PBPH revoked · SK Menhut 971/2026 dated 19 Nov · company says 41,000+ workers · about 18,363 ha oil palm in concession · 541 ha unpermitted mining · 212 ha protected area damage
events.why_it_matters: A huge pulp-and-paper operation and tens of thousands of jobs shift to state-linked control.

events.event: Labour group KSPI estimates layoff (PHK) victims could exceed 90,000 people by end-2026, with textiles hardest hit, while a Liputan6 tally cites about 72,000 in 2026 so far.
events.key_numbers: KSPI estimate 90,000+ by end-2026 · Liputan6 count about 72,000 (2026 YTD) · textile industry most affected
events.why_it_matters: Job losses are the clearest sign of household pressure behind the market slump.
